```{python}
def rcoef_p(resp, term):

def n_sig_scr(resp, a=alpha):

def n_sig_rsm(resp, a=alpha):
    d = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, resp)
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Protein A chromatography is the capture step of the A-Mab drug substance process and the
first chromatographic operation in the purification train. The step binds A-Mab from the
clarified harvest on an immobilized Protein A resin, removes host cell protein (HCP) and DNA in the flow-through and the wash, and elutes the antibody at low pH into the low-pH viral
inactivation step. Characterization was executed under the paired plan PCP-005 on a
scale-down model qualified against manufacturing-scale performance (SOP-1001). The work was executed to the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011], to the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11] and to the risk basis recorded in RA-001. Commercial manufacture of the drug substance runs at
`{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L [@amab2009].

In total `{python} n_params` process parameters were assessed at this step. Of these,
`{python} n_multi` were studied in a two-level factorial screening design of `{python} n_scr` runs and
then in a face-centred central composite design of `{python} n_rsm` runs, while the
remaining `{python} n_uni` (operating temperature and bed height) were assessed one
parameter at a time. On the evidence set out in §9, `{python} n_wccpp` parameters were
classified as well-controlled critical process parameters, `{python} n_kpp` as key process
parameters and `{python} n_gpp` as general process parameters. No parameter at this step
was classified as a critical process parameter.

The step sets one critical quality attribute, leached Protein A, and is the principal
clearance step for host cell protein and residual DNA (§2.2). Pool host cell protein is
the response that bounds the operating region. Because the response-surface model for that
response is adequate and predictive (R² = `{python} f"{fits_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['R2']:.3f}"`,
adjusted R² = `{python} f"{fits_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['adjR2']:.3f}"`, predicted R² =
`{python} f"{fits_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['predR2']:.3f}"`), the design space in §6 is
derived from it. Over the characterized region, the model places `{python} pct(1 - ds_frac)` of the evaluated settings above the in-process limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ipc:,.0f}"` ng/mg. The same limit was exceeded by `{python} n_pool_over` of the `{python} n_pools` pools assayed across the two designs, every one of them at the low edge of the elution pH range. The settings that produced those pools mark an edge of failure for the step.

The normal operating range is not wholly inside the acceptable region. That range includes a corner at `{python} nor_corner_txt`, where the model predicts `{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst:,.0f}"` ng/mg against a limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ipc:,.0f}"` ng/mg. However, the in-process limit itself carries an
assurance factor of `{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"` below the pool concentration above which
the downstream train can no longer bring a batch to specification. Even at that corner the drug substance would carry `{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst_ds:.0f}"` ng/mg against a
specification of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"` ng/mg. The operating region is therefore
stated in §6 as a joint constraint on protein load and elution buffer pH.

Leached Protein A produced no model of predictive value. Neither the screening fit nor the response-surface model reaches significance (p = `{python} f"{fits_scr['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p']:.2f}"` and p = `{python} f"{fits_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p']:.2f}"`), with a negative predicted coefficient of determination in both cases. For this reason the
claim for this attribute is made from the assayed pools without a model. All `{python} n_pools` pools met the acceptance criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm, and the highest of them reached `{python} f"{lpa_max:.2f}"` ppm.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches operated within the normal operating range, and all three attributes this step governs meet the drug-substance criteria (§8). The tightest of the three attributes is `{python} cpk_tight_name`, at Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_tight:.1f}"` against a limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"` ng/mg, with a simulated mean of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg. Two deviations were recorded during execution and
are reported in §13. Both were investigated, dispositioned as retained and assessed as
having no effect on the fitted models, on the operating region or on the classifications.

The step therefore delivers a bounded operating region for the two parameters that govern
pool host cell protein, a leached Protein A level inside the criterion at every setting studied and the capture-stage share of host cell protein and DNA clearance. Protein A
chromatography does not by itself bring host cell protein to the drug-substance
specification. The remaining clearance is delivered by cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008), while no viral clearance is claimed for this step. These results are rolled up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that is manufactured by fed-batch mammalian cell culture and purified on an established platform train [@amab2009]. The train runs Protein
A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small-virus
retentive filtration and ultrafiltration with diafiltration. Protein A chromatography is
Step `{python} step_no` of that train and the first purification step after harvest and
clarification (PCR-004).

The step is operated in bind and elute mode on an immobilized Protein A affinity resin.
Clarified harvest is loaded at `{python} f"{SP['load']:g}"` g/L resin onto a bed of
`{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('bed_height').setpoint:g}"` cm at a linear velocity of `{python} f"{SP['flow']:g}"` cm/hr. The antibody binds through the Fc region while
host cell protein, DNA and media components pass into the flow-through and are further
reduced by the post-load wash. Bound antibody is released by a low-pH elution buffer at pH
`{python} f"{SP['elution_ph']:g}"`, with the eluate collected to
`{python} f"{SP['end_collect']:g}"` column volumes on the descending edge of the peak.
Because the low-pH eluate is also the feed to the viral inactivation step, the elution
condition serves two purposes at once.

Three impurity attributes are governed here. Leached Protein A is formed at this step and
at no other, since it is the affinity ligand released from the resin under the elution
condition. Host cell protein and residual DNA are formed in the production bioreactor
(PCR-003) and are cleared here for the first time. Product quality attributes formed
upstream, such as the glycan and charge variants, pass through the step unaltered, because
affinity capture does not discriminate between them [@amab2009].

## Objectives

This report records the executed characterization of Step `{python} step_no` and has five
objectives:

(i) quantify the relationship between each studied parameter and the responses that
matter at this step, namely pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A;

(ii) define the multivariate operating region over which the governed attributes remain
within their criteria;

(iii) establish proven acceptable ranges for each parameter against each governed
attribute;

(iv) classify every parameter of the step against the decision logic in SOP-4001; and

(v) justify the Stage 2 ranges and the contribution this step makes to the control
strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The study is a Stage 1 process design activity in the sense of the lifecycle guidance
[@fda2011]. The record of that study is the evidence that the commercial ranges proposed for this step rest on data and on prior knowledge instead of on the transfer of a set-point alone.
The design space concept used in §6 is supplied by ICH Q8, the risk methodology carried forward from RA-001 by ICH Q9 and the framing of the control strategy in §10 by ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11].

Criticality is treated as a continuum in this package. Attributes are assigned a level of
very low, low, moderate, high or very high, of which the levels high and very high are
called critical [@amab2009]. Parameter classes follow the same logic: a well-controlled critical process parameter is one whose variability affects a critical quality attribute
but which carries a low risk of leaving the design space, whereas a critical process
parameter carries a high risk of leaving it. Since that distinction rests on control
capability and on the size of the region as well as on the size of the effect, it is
applied at the end of this report (§9) and not at the start.

No viral clearance claim is made for the Protein A step. The modular clearance claim for
A-Mab rests on low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and small-virus retentive filtration, all consolidated in PCMR-001 under ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a].

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The Protein A capture step is a platform operation at Novacyte Biologics with an extensive
performance history. It has been used to manufacture three earlier humanized IgG1 products
(X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and to supply the A-Mab clinical programme. Across that experience the step has recovered antibody consistently and has reduced host cell protein
and DNA by a large factor at every scale operated. This body of experience reduced the
amount of development work the present study had to do. Characterization at this step
confirms and bounds behaviour that is already understood rather than discovering it, which is the same argument the case study makes for its own downstream platform [@amab2009]. The transfer of that credit is justified by mechanism rather than by similarity alone, because the resin chemistry, the bed geometry and the buffer system used for A-Mab are the platform ones, with the antibody itself the only material difference between A-Mab and the earlier products at this step.

The mechanistic expectations the study set out to test were also supplied by prior knowledge.
Elution buffer pH was expected to be the dominant parameter for pool host cell protein,
because the pH of the elution buffer determines which of the impurities bound to the resin
and to the product desorb together with the antibody. Protein load was expected to act in
the opposite direction: as the load approaches the dynamic binding capacity of the resin,
the mass-transfer zone extends further down the bed and a greater share of the loaded
impurity burden is carried into the eluate. The two parameters were expected to interact,
since the impurity recruited by a heavy load and the impurity recruited by an aggressive
elution are partly the same material.

Step yield was expected to be governed by the end of pool collect, which sets how far down
the descending edge of the elution peak the pool is taken. Load flow rate acts on yield
through residence time in the bed, since a high linear velocity shortens contact and
increases breakthrough during the load phase, and that effect was expected to be strongest when the bed is already heavily loaded.

Leaching of the affinity ligand was expected to be a property of the resin and of the
elution condition, and to be small enough over the proposed ranges to be hard to resolve.
Leached Protein A is assigned by the platform to the resin life-cycle programme (SOP-2008) as much as to the operating parameters, because ligand release accumulates with cycle number and sanitization history. The analysis reported in §5.3 was framed by that expectation.

## Quality attributes in scope

One critical quality attribute is set by this step: leached Protein A, a process impurity of low to moderate criticality. The acceptance criterion for that attribute is given in @tbl-cqa-set with the Tool #1 score, which is the product of impact and uncertainty in the criticality assessment [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print("\n: The critical quality attribute set by Step 5. {#tbl-cqa-set}\n")
```

Two further attributes are governed at this step without being formed here, with all three listed together in @tbl-cqa-gov in the order they are discussed below.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["leached_protein_a", "hcp", "residual_dna"]))
print("\n: Quality attributes governed at Step 5, with acceptance criteria and "
      "criticality. {#tbl-cqa-gov}\n")
```

Host cell protein is the most consequential of the three, at moderate to high criticality,
because it is the impurity present in the largest amount in the clarified harvest and
because it carries the highest Tool #1 score in @tbl-cqa-gov. The second of the three,
leached Protein A, is of low to moderate criticality and is the one attribute this step
adds instead of removing. The third, residual DNA, is of very low criticality and is cleared by a wide margin over the train as a whole.

The acceptance criteria in @tbl-cqa-gov apply to the drug substance and not to the Protein
A pool. An intermediate has to be judged against a criterion that applies to an intermediate. For this reason the two criteria this report uses are defined in §7. In outline, pool host cell protein is judged against an in-process limit carried back from the drug-substance criterion through the clearance the polishing steps deliver. Leached Protein A keeps the drug-substance criterion itself, which is the conservative choice at a capture step.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

Every Protein A process parameter was assessed in RA-001 by risk ranking and filtering, each of them scored on potential impact to quality attributes and on potential interaction with other parameters [@amab2009]. Parameters were placed into three groups by that assessment: those
warranting multivariate evaluation, those whose ranges could be supported by a univariate study and those needing no new study because platform ranges already cover them. That grouping is the scope this report executes. For each of the six parameters the outcome is recorded in @tbl-params.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_multi` were carried into the multivariate designs: protein load,
elution buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect. Protein load and elution buffer pH were selected on the strength of the expected effect on pool host cell protein, while load flow rate and end of pool collect were selected on the expected effect on step yield and on the
load by flow interaction the platform had already seen. All four were expected to
interact, which is the condition under which a univariate study cannot support a range
(PDA TR 60 makes the same point about one-factor-at-a-time experimentation).

Operating temperature and bed height were assigned to univariate assessment, since neither acts on the binding chemistry of the step: temperature affects the kinetics of adsorption and
the stability of the eluted antibody over a narrow band, and bed height acts through
residence time at a fixed linear velocity. Both are held to platform ranges by equipment
design and are readily controlled, which is why a one-at-a-time assessment was judged
sufficient for them in RA-001.

The ranges themselves were set wider than the routine control ranges so that the study
would describe the process over a knowledge space instead of only at the operating point.
Each characterization range in @tbl-params is at least
`{python} f"{range_ratio_min:.1f}"` times the width of the corresponding normal
operating range. The wider ranges also provide the process understanding that is needed to support later movement within the design space.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

A scale-down chromatography system was qualified as a model of the manufacturing-scale
step under SOP-1001. The model was designed on the established principles of
chromatographic scaling, holding bed height, linear velocity, residence time, load in
grams per litre of resin and all buffer volumes normalized to column volumes at their
commercial-equivalent values, and column efficiency was verified before each campaign by
plate count and peak asymmetry. Runs were executed in the temperature-controlled
chromatography chamber EQ-CHR-118, which was within the calibration interval throughout execution and is next due on `{python} eq_chr_118_cal_due`.

The scale-down model was compared with manufacturing-scale performance on the attributes that matter for the claims in this report: step yield, pool volume, pool host
cell protein and leached Protein A. No difference of practical consequence between the scales was found. The qualification record is filed under SOP-1001, with the model treated as representative for the purpose of defining operating ranges and of supporting the clearance contribution stated in §10. However, a qualification of this kind bounds what the model may be used for. It supports claims about the operating ranges and about the clearance a single cycle delivers, without saying anything about how the resin behaves after many cycles, which is why the resin life-cycle is addressed separately in §11.

Centre-point replicates provide the pure-error term against which lack of fit is tested.
The centre points were executed at the set-point condition, `{python} cp_scr` of them in the screening design and `{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design. The spread of those replicates is reported in §5.1 and used in the lack-of-fit partition in §5.3.

## Operation

Each run was executed to the operating sequence of SOP-2007: equilibration, load, post-load wash,
low-pH elution with pool collection on the descending edge, strip, sanitization and
storage. Only the four studied parameters were allowed to vary. Every other setting was held at the
commercial-equivalent value, including the wash composition, the equilibration volume and
the sanitization sequence.

Materials controlled to platform specification were verified for identity and quality and
were not characterized in this study. Resin lots were qualified before use and were tracked under SOP-2008, which also governs packing, cycle counting and sanitization. Buffers were
prepared and released against a pH and conductivity specification before use, a control
that is directly relevant to the deviation reported in §13.1. The clarified harvest used
as feed was drawn from material characterized in PCR-004.

## Analytical methods

Every response and every released attribute was measured by a validated method.
The controlled documents that govern this step are listed in @tbl-methods, with the performance figures for the two methods that carry the quantitative claims given in Appendix D.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=PROTEIN_A_SOP_REFS, amvs=PROTEIN_A_AMV_REFS))
print("\n: Controlled procedures and validated analytical methods for Step 5. "
      "{#tbl-methods}\n")
```

Pool host cell protein was measured by ELISA under AMV-3012 and is reported as ng of host
cell protein per mg of antibody. Leached Protein A was measured by ELISA under AMV-3016
and is reported in ppm, residual DNA by qPCR under AMV-3014 and size variants by SEC-HPLC under AMV-3011. Step yield was calculated from the
antibody mass loaded and the antibody mass recovered in the eluate pool.

The two ELISA methods differ in precision by a wide margin, which matters for the interpretation of §5.1 and §5.3.
AMV-3012 has an intermediate precision of `{python} f"{hcp_prec:g}"` %RSD and AMV-3016 has
`{python} f"{lpa_prec:g}"` %RSD, against observed effects that differ in relative size by about an order of magnitude between the two attributes. The share of total observed
variance attributable to each assay is given in Appendix D and is used in §5.1 to separate
analytical scatter from process variation.

## Sampling plan

Samples were taken from the load, the flow-through, the pooled wash and the eluate pool on
every run. The eluate pool was assayed for host cell protein, leached Protein A, residual
DNA and size variants, while the load and flow-through samples support the mass balance
behind the reported step yield.

The centre-point condition was executed `{python} cp_scr` times in the screening design
and `{python} cp_rsm` times in the response-surface design, giving
`{python} cp_scr + cp_rsm` independent replicates of the set-point across the campaign.
All runs within a design were executed in randomized order under SOP-1002.

## Statistical methods

Factors were coded so that the midpoint of each characterization range is zero and the
edges are −1 and +1. At this step the midpoint of every characterization range coincides with the set-point of the parameter. Therefore the coded origin and the set-point condition are one and the same.

The screening data were analysed as an ordinary least-squares model in the four main
effects and the six two-factor interactions, with an effect reported as twice the
coefficient on the coded factor. The response-surface data were analysed as a full
quadratic model in the same four factors, which gives `{python} n_terms_rsm` terms and
leaves `{python} df_res_rsm` residual degrees of freedom. Significance is judged at
α = `{python} alpha` throughout.

Model adequacy is reported as the coefficient of determination, the adjusted coefficient,
the predicted coefficient computed from the PRESS statistic, the model F ratio with the associated p-value, and lack of fit is tested by partitioning the residual sum of squares into a
lack-of-fit component and the pure error from the centre-point replicates. A response for
which no factor reaches significance is treated as robust over the ranges studied, in
which case the factors are kept in the knowledge space as evidence of that robustness.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches with every parameter drawn inside the normal operating range, and is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the drug-substance criterion. The proven acceptable ranges in §7 are computed from the same fitted response-surface models, in the two forms described there.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

All `{python} n_params` parameters of the step are given in @tbl-params with the
set-points, normal operating ranges, characterization ranges, study type and final
classification. The characterization
range is the knowledge-space edge of each parameter and is not itself a proven acceptable
range; the proven acceptable ranges are computed per attribute in §7.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
print("\n: Process parameters of Step 5, with set-point, normal operating range, "
      "characterization range, study type and final classification. {#tbl-params}\n")
```

The letters used for the coded factors in the effect and coefficient tables are given in
@tbl-legend. All four multivariate parameters appear in both designs, which means that the same letter is used for the same factor throughout this report.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print("\n: Coded factor legend for the screening and response-surface designs. "
      "{#tbl-legend}\n")
```

The range of each factor was justified against prior knowledge instead of being set as a
fixed multiple of the routine range. Protein load runs from
`{python} f"{PR['load'][0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{PR['load'][1]:g}"` g/L resin, which spans
the region from a lightly loaded column to a load approaching the dynamic binding capacity
of the resin. Elution buffer pH runs from `{python} f"{PR['elution_ph'][0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{PR['elution_ph'][1]:g}"`, covering the band over which the antibody desorbs
completely at the low edge and incompletely at the high edge. Load flow rate runs from
`{python} f"{PR['flow'][0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{PR['flow'][1]:g}"` cm/hr, which is the velocity range the commercial column can deliver. End of pool collect runs from
`{python} f"{PR['end_collect'][0]:g}"` to `{python} f"{PR['end_collect'][1]:g}"` column
volumes, which brackets the descending edge of the elution peak.

## Screening design

The screening was executed as a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate factors with `{python} cp_scr` centre points, giving `{python} n_scr` runs in total. A full factorial in
four factors estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction without
aliasing, which a fractional design of the same size could not do. The resulting model carries `{python} n_terms_scr` terms against `{python} df_res_scr` residual degrees of freedom, which is a near-saturated fit. The purpose of the screening stage is to identify which factors matter, with the coded settings and the measured responses of all `{python} n_scr` runs given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design was a face-centred central composite design in the same four
factors, with `{python} n_fact_rsm` factorial runs, `{python} n_axial_rsm` axial runs and
`{python} cp_rsm` centre points, giving `{python} n_rsm` runs. Because the axial points sit
on the faces of the coded cube, every run stayed inside the characterization ranges of
@tbl-params and no run required a setting outside the knowledge space. The added axial
points estimate the four quadratic terms, which is what turns a set of resolved effects
into a predictive surface. The face-centred form was chosen in preference to a rotatable design for a practical reason: a rotatable central composite in four factors places the axial points beyond the cube, and settings outside the characterization ranges of @tbl-params would have taken the study outside the knowledge space RA-001 authorized. The response-surface model is the predictive model of this report and the basis of the design space in §6, with the design matrix and the measured responses given in Appendix B.

Both designs were executed on the same scale-down configuration and with the same feed
material, which makes the two datasets directly comparable. Neither design was invalidated
or re-executed. Because the deviations recorded in §13 were dispositioned as retained, every run executed under this plan is included in the analysis reported below.

## Univariate assessment

Operating temperature and bed height were assessed one parameter at a time over the
characterization ranges in @tbl-params, with the other parameters held at the set-point.
Neither was included in the multivariate designs, for the reasons given in §2.3. Both were
classified as general process parameters (@tbl-params). Under SOP-4001 a general process
parameter is one whose variation over the range studied was not linked to a critical quality attribute. The classification rationale for the two parameters is set out in §9.

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The centre-point replicates set the precision against which every effect in this section is judged, and the three responses differ sharply in that precision. The mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation of each response over the `{python} cp_rsm` centre points of the response-surface design are given in @tbl-cv-rsm.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm"))
print("\n: Centre-point reproducibility in the response-surface design, and the pure-error "
      "basis for the lack-of-fit tests in §5.3. {#tbl-cv-rsm}\n")
```

Step yield is the most reproducible response, at `{python} f"{cvr('step_yield'):.1f}"` %, with pool host cell protein next at `{python} f"{cvr('pool_hcp_ng_mg'):.1f}"` %, which
is small against effects that run to several thousand ng/mg. Leached Protein A is the least precise of the three by a wide margin, at a coefficient of variation of `{python} f"{cvr('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.1f}"` % over the same `{python} cp_rsm` replicates (@tbl-cv-rsm). That coefficient of variation is larger than the validated intermediate precision of AMV-3016
alone would produce (`{python} f"{lpa_prec:g}"` %RSD, Appendix D). Run-to-run variation in
ligand release therefore contributes to the centre-point spread alongside the assay.

The screening design gives a second, independent read of the same condition, which is reported in @tbl-cv-scr over `{python} cp_scr` replicates.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening"))
print("\n: Centre-point reproducibility in the screening design. {#tbl-cv-scr}\n")
```

Both designs place step yield as the most reproducible response (@tbl-cv-rsm, @tbl-cv-scr), although they disagree on pool host cell protein, where the screening centre points scatter at
`{python} f"{cvr('pool_hcp_ng_mg', 'screening'):.1f}"` % against
`{python} f"{cvr('pool_hcp_ng_mg'):.1f}"` % in the response-surface design. With only `{python} cp_scr` replicates the screening estimate is itself imprecise, which is why the lack-of-fit tests in §5.3 use the response-surface pure error.

## Screening: factor effects

The factors that govern pool host cell protein and step yield were resolved in the screening stage. By contrast, nothing at all was resolved for leached Protein A. The fit of each screening model is given in @tbl-fit-scr.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening"))
print("\n: Screening model fit for the three responses. {#tbl-fit-scr}\n")
```

The models for pool host cell protein and step yield fit well, whereas the model for
leached Protein A does not. Pool host cell protein and step yield
reach R² of `{python} f"{fits_scr['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['R2']:.3f}"` and
`{python} f"{fits_scr['step_yield']['R2']:.3f}"` with model p-values below
α = `{python} alpha`, whereas leached Protein A reaches R² =
`{python} f"{fits_scr['leached_protein_a_ppm']['R2']:.3f}"` with an adjusted R² of
`{python} f"{fits_scr['leached_protein_a_ppm']['adjR2']:.3f}"` and a model p-value of
`{python} f"{fits_scr['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p']:.2f}"`. A negative adjusted
coefficient on a near-saturated fit means the terms explain less than their degrees of
freedom cost, which is the signature of a null result.

Pool host cell protein was affected by elution buffer pH, by protein load and by the
interaction between them. The effect estimates for pool host cell protein are given in @tbl-eff-hcp, in descending order of magnitude.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", top=6))
print("\n: Screening effect estimates for pool host cell protein, the six largest by "
```

Raising elution buffer pH across the characterized range lowered pool host cell protein by
`{python} f"{abs(eff('pool_hcp_ng_mg','B')):,.0f}"` ng/mg, while raising protein load
raised it by `{python} f"{eff('pool_hcp_ng_mg','A'):,.0f}"` ng/mg. Both effects are large against a centre-point standard deviation of a few hundred ng/mg, at p < `{python} alpha`. The third of the significant effects is the load by pH interaction, at `{python} f"{eff('pool_hcp_ng_mg','AB'):,.0f}"` ng/mg (p =
`{python} f"{eff_p('pool_hcp_ng_mg','AB'):.3f}"`). The negative sign means that the penalty for loading heavily is smaller when the elution is run at the high end of the pH range.
`{python} n_sig_scr('pool_hcp_ng_mg')` of the `{python} n_terms_scr` terms reach significance, with every term involving load flow rate among the `{python} n_terms_scr - n_sig_scr('pool_hcp_ng_mg')` that do not.

Step yield was affected by more factors and by smaller amounts. The dominant factor for step yield is end of pool collect, at `{python} f"{eff('step_yield','D'):.3f}"`, which is a gain of about
`{python} f"{100*eff('step_yield','D'):.1f}"` percentage points of yield across the
collect range. Protein load and load flow rate each reduce yield, by
`{python} f"{abs(eff('step_yield','A')):.3f}"` and
`{python} f"{abs(eff('step_yield','C')):.3f}"` respectively, and the interaction between them is significant at `{python} f"{eff('step_yield','AC'):.3f}"` (p =
`{python} f"{eff_p('step_yield','AC'):.4f}"`). The six largest estimates for step yield are given in @tbl-eff-yield.

Leached Protein A returned no significant term at all. In @tbl-eff-lpa the largest of the
six estimates is the load by flow interaction, at
`{python} f"{eff('leached_protein_a_ppm','AC'):.3f}"` ppm with a p-value of
`{python} f"{eff_p('leached_protein_a_ppm','AC'):.2f}"`.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", top=6))
print("\n: Screening effect estimates for leached Protein A, the six largest by magnitude. "
      "None reaches significance. {#tbl-eff-lpa}\n")
```

Every estimate in @tbl-eff-lpa is smaller than the centre-point standard deviation of the
same response. No factor could therefore be separated from the run-to-run noise on this
design. That null result is informative in itself. The four factors stay in the knowledge space as evidence that ligand release is insensitive to them over the ranges screened, which is the basis on which they are classified in §9.

These effect magnitudes identify which factors matter, but they are not the predictive model of this report, because a near-saturated two-level fit with `{python} df_res_scr` residual degrees of freedom can neither separate curvature from error nor predict at an interior point of the region. Those estimates are refined by the response-surface models in §5.3.

The response-surface stage produced one model that is adequate and predictive, one that is

Pool host cell protein is modelled well. The full quadratic model reaches R² =

`{python} f"{fits_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['adjR2']:.3f}"` and predicted R² =

is adequate but less predictive, at R² =

Leached Protein A yielded no usable model. The quadratic fit reaches R² = `{python} f"{fits_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['R2']:.3f}"` (@tbl-fit-rsm), but the adjusted coefficient falls to `{python} f"{fits_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['adjR2']:.3f}"` and the predicted

The fitted surfaces are shown in @fig-surfaces over protein load and elution buffer pH,


The leached Protein A model is retained as knowledge-space evidence and is put to no other use in this report. The diagnostics for that model are given in @fig-diag-lpa. Exactly one of the

that many terms at α = `{python} alpha` produces by chance. Lack of fit is far from significant (p = `{python} f"{fits_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p_lof']:.2f}"`, Appendix C). That test compares the residual with the pure error. The pure error for this response is large (`{python} f"{cvr('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.1f}"` % at the centre point). A

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-lpa
#| fig-cap: "Model diagnostics for leached Protein A. The actual against predicted panel shows the scatter that a predicted R-squared below zero describes."
```

The operative claim for leached Protein A is therefore made from the assayed pools
directly. Across the `{python} n_pools` runs of the two designs, the pools ranged from
`{python} f"{lpa_min:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{lpa_max:.2f}"` ppm, with a mean of `{python} f"{lpa_mean:.2f}"` ppm and a standard deviation of `{python} f"{lpa_sd:.2f}"` ppm, against an acceptance criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm, which `{python} f"{n_pools - lpa_over}"` of them met. The highest single pool left
`{python} f"{lpa_head:.2f}"` ppm of margin, which is narrow on one run and is the reason
the attribute is monitored on every batch (§10). However, the criterion applied here is the drug-substance specification, which is applied to the capture pool conservatively. Leached Protein A is cleared downstream of this step by cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-007, PCR-008). In addition, only `{python} f"{lpa_ds_mean:.3f}"` ppm of leached Protein A is carried by the simulated drug substance at commercial scale (§8).

## Mechanistic interpretation

The surfaces in @fig-surfaces follow from the physical chemistry of affinity capture and confirm the expectations recorded in §2.1. Elution buffer pH governs pool host cell
protein because it sets the aggressiveness of desorption: a lower pH releases the antibody
faster and also releases the more tightly associated host cell protein, which then
co-elutes into the collected pool. The convex quadratic term means the effect is not uniform across the range: host cell protein falls steeply as pH rises from the low edge
and then flattens above the set-point, which leaves the pool most sensitive to pH exactly
where the pH is lowest.

Protein load acts through the capacity of the bed: at a light load the antibody occupies a small fraction of the available ligand and the impurity that binds non-specifically is
washed away efficiently, whereas a load approaching dynamic binding capacity extends the
mass-transfer zone and retains a greater share of the loaded impurity into the elution.
The negative interaction between load and pH follows directly: at a high elution pH part of the impurity recruited by a heavy load is left behind on the resin in any case, which makes the two effects less than additive over the characterized ranges.

Step yield is governed by where the pool is stopped. Collecting further down the
descending edge recovers antibody that would otherwise go to strip, which is why end of pool collect carries the dominant positive term. By contrast, load and flow act in the opposite direction through breakthrough during the load phase. The interaction between them is negative (@tbl-eff-yield) because a short residence time matters most when the bed is already close to saturation.

Leaching of the affinity ligand behaves as a resin property over these ranges, since ligand release depends on the chemistry of the immobilization, on the cumulative cycle count and
on the sanitization history, none of which is a parameter of a single run. Nothing in the data contradicts that account. The four operating parameters together explain no more of the pool variation than chance would, while the centre-point replicates scatter more widely than any factor moved the response.

These results also explain why a multivariate region is required in place of four
independent ranges. The two parameters that bound the operating region interact, with the surface curved in one of them. A univariate range for protein load would have to be set at the load that is acceptable at the worst elution pH. A univariate range for elution pH would have to be set at the pH that is acceptable at the heaviest load. Consequently, both would be narrower than the process needs, whereas the multivariate region in §6 states the constraint the process actually faces.

# Design space

The design space for Step `{python} step_no` is defined as the region in protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect over which the fitted response-surface models
predict a pool host cell protein at or below `{python} f"{hcp_ipc:,.0f}"` ng/mg and a
leached Protein A at or below `{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm. Evaluated on an even grid
of `{python} f"{ds_n:,}"` settings across the characterized ranges,
`{python} pct(ds_frac)` of the region meets both criteria. The binding constraint on that region is `{python} ds_binding`, since leached Protein A rejects `{python} pct(ds_rej_lpa)` of the grid on its own.

The principal plane of the region is protein load against elution buffer pH (the plane drawn in @fig-surfaces). Load flow rate and end of pool collect do not bound the region within the characterized ranges. The role of load flow rate and end of pool collect in the control strategy is to govern step yield (§10). At the set-point the model predicts
`{python} f"{hcp_sp:,.0f}"` ng/mg, which is `{python} f"{hcp_sp_ratio:.2f}"`-fold below
the in-process limit.

The worst case predicted by the same model within the characterized region is the corner at `{python} par_corner_txt`, at `{python} f"{hcp_par_worst:,.0f}"` ng/mg. That corner lies far outside the design space
and is an edge of failure for the step rather than a setting the process may take.
`{python} n_pool_over` of the `{python} n_pools` executed runs produced a pool above the in-process limit, all `{python} n_pool_over_lowph` of them at the low edge of the elution pH range. Those runs are the direct experimental evidence for where the boundary
lies.

The normal operating range is not wholly contained in the design space, and that gap has to be stated plainly. `{python} pct(1 - nor_ok)` of the settings inside the normal operating
range exceed the in-process limit on the fitted model, the worst of them being the corner
at `{python} nor_corner_txt`, at which the model predicts
`{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst:,.0f}"` ng/mg. Three considerations bound what that means. The
in-process limit is itself set `{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"`-fold below the pool
concentration of `{python} f"{hcp_ceiling:,.0f}"` ng/mg at which the downstream train
would no longer bring a batch into specification, which makes an excursion above the limit
an alert instead of a batch failure. At that same corner the batch would still reach specification, with the drug substance at `{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst_ds:.0f}"` ng/mg against a limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"` ng/mg, on the clearance the two polishing steps deliver in the nominal train. And the corner requires both parameters to sit at an unfavourable edge
at the same time.

The operative constraint is therefore a joint one. Protein load and elution buffer pH must
be held so that the pair lies inside the region, with neither read as an independent range at its own edge. At the top of the load normal operating range,
`{python} f"{NOR['load'][1]:g}"` g/L resin, elution buffer pH must be at least `{python} f"{ph_at_load_hi:.2f}"` with the other two factors at their set-points. That
value sits above the low edge of the pH normal operating range,
`{python} f"{NOR['elution_ph'][0]:g}"`, which is the same finding expressed as a pH.

Movement within the design space is not considered a change in the sense of ICH Q8, although all changes remain subject to the pharmaceutical quality system (ICH Q10). Movement outside the design space requires change control with a supporting assessment [@ichq8; @ichq10]. Three bounds apply to the
claim. The region is defined only over the characterization ranges in @tbl-params and says
nothing about settings beyond them. The models predict mean levels and carry no interval, which is why the assurance form of the claim is the NOR-propagated analysis in §7. And the whole region rests on the scale-down model qualified in §3.1, which was qualified on performance attributes and not on resin life-cycle behaviour. In practice the region is used in two ways: a proposed change to a set-point or a range is checked against the region before execution, and any excursion recorded during manufacture is assessed against it as part of the batch disposition.

# Proven acceptable ranges

The proven acceptable ranges complement the multivariate region with a per-attribute,
per-parameter view. Since the acceptance basis differs between the two governed responses,
and since the ranges cannot be read without knowing which criterion produced them, the two
criteria are defined before the table. Pool host cell protein is judged against an
`{python} hcp_basis` limit of `{python} f"{hcp_ipc:,.0f}"` ng/mg, carried back from the
drug-substance criterion of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"` ng/mg through the clearance
credited to cation exchange (`{python} f"{cex_fold:.0f}"`-fold) and anion exchange
(`{python} f"{aex_fold:.1f}"`-fold), then divided by an assurance factor of
`{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"`. Leached Protein A has no in-process limit configured and is
judged against the `{python} lpa_basis` criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm directly.

Both analyses are given in @tbl-par for every governed attribute and every multivariate parameter, and the first column of ranges holds the other three factors at their set-points. The second propagates the normal operating range of the other three by Monte-Carlo of the fitted model and requires the 95 % predictive interval to stay within the criterion, which makes it a robustness statement instead of a mean-level one.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(PAR)
print("\n: Proven acceptable ranges per governed attribute and parameter, at set-point and "
      "with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges. {#tbl-par}\n")
```

Leached Protein A is acceptable across the whole characterization range of every parameter
under the at-set-point analysis, and under NOR propagation for three of the four. The one
exception is elution buffer pH, whose NOR-propagated range narrows to
`{python} par_cell('leached_protein_a_ppm','elution_ph','PAR (NOR)')` against a
characterization range of
`{python} par_cell('leached_protein_a_ppm','elution_ph','Char. range')`. The excluded
sliver lies at the high pH edge and follows from the quadratic term discussed in §5.3,
which the analysis propagates because it is in the fitted model. Given that the model
explains no more than chance, this narrowing should be read as an artefact of propagating
a null model instead of as a demonstrated pH effect. Over the whole normal operating range
the same model predicts a maximum of `{python} f"{nor_lpa_max:.2f}"` ppm.

Pool host cell protein behaves differently, and the NOR-propagated ranges for that response are the binding result of this section. Under the at-set-point analysis three parameters are acceptable across their whole characterization ranges and elution buffer pH is acceptable from
`{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','elution_ph','PAR (set-point)')`. Under NOR propagation every range narrows: protein load to `{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','load','PAR (NOR)')` g/L resin against a normal operating range of `{python} f"{NOR['load'][0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{NOR['load'][1]:g}"`, and elution buffer pH to
`{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','elution_ph','PAR (NOR)')` against a normal operating
range of
`{python} f"{NOR['elution_ph'][0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{NOR['elution_ph'][1]:g}"`. Neither of
the two proven acceptable ranges covers the whole of the corresponding routine range.

That result is the univariate expression of the design-space finding in §6 and carries the
same consequence. The upper part of the load normal operating range is proven only when elution buffer pH sits above the low part of the pH range. In the same way, the low part of the pH range is proven only at a load below the top of the load range. Load flow rate and end of
pool collect behave differently again. Both of the NOR-propagated ranges,
`{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','flow','PAR (NOR)')` cm/hr and
`{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','end_collect','PAR (NOR)')` CV, contain the whole of the corresponding normal operating range. As a result, neither of the two constrains the operating region.

The governing parameter for pool host cell protein is shown in @fig-par-hcp and the governing parameter for leached Protein A in @fig-par-lpa. In each figure the acceptable region is shaded, the acceptance limit is drawn and the set-point and normal operating range are marked.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for pool host cell protein against elution buffer pH, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
_ = D.fig_par(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", D.governing_factor(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-lpa
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range for leached Protein A against protein load, at set-point (left) and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges (right)."
_ = D.fig_par(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", D.governing_factor(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"))
plt.show()
```

The relationship between these ranges and the design space should be read in one direction
only. A proven acceptable range is a univariate or NOR-robust statement about one
parameter, whereas the design space of §6 is the multivariate region. Where a whole
characterization range is proven acceptable, as it is for leached Protein A against three
parameters, the binding constraint on the operating region is the multivariate corner and
not any univariate range. Where a proven acceptable range is narrower than the routine
range, as it is for protein load and elution buffer pH against pool host cell protein, the
narrower result governs. Both statements are bounded by the characterization ranges in @tbl-params and by the fitted models of §5.3. Both analyses also share the limitation of the model they are computed from, since a proven acceptable range derived from a fitted surface can be no more reliable than that surface, which is why the leached Protein A rows of @tbl-par are reported without being relied on.

# Process capability and robustness

Capability at commercial scale was estimated by drawing `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated
batches with every parameter distributed inside the normal operating range and propagating them through the process model. The resulting distribution of each governed attribute is reported in @tbl-cap against the drug-substance criterion, as a one-sided Cpk. Because the simulation propagates parameter variation through the fitted models of every step in the train, those figures are a statement about the process as a whole and not about this step alone.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(["hcp", "residual_dna", "leached_protein_a"]))
print("\n: Commercial-scale capability of the attributes governed at Step 5, from "
      "Monte-Carlo simulation of NOR-bounded batches. {#tbl-cap}\n")
```

Host cell protein is the tightest of the three, at Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_hcp:.1f}"`. The simulated mean is `{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg with a standard deviation of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_sd:.1f}"`. The largest of the `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` simulated batches reached `{python} f"{hcp_ds_max:.1f}"` ng/mg against a specification of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"` ng/mg. That capability is not delivered by this step alone: Protein A capture takes the harvest burden down to about
`{python} f"{hcp_nom:,.0f}"` ng/mg in the nominal train, after which cation exchange
(PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008) contribute
`{python} f"{cex_fold:.0f}"`-fold and `{python} f"{aex_fold:.1f}"`-fold in turn.

The other two attributes sit far from the limits. Residual DNA reaches Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_dna:.1f}"` (@tbl-cap), with this step contributing
`{python} f"{dna_lrv:g}"` log₁₀ of clearance and anion exchange contributing the rest
(PCR-008). Leached Protein A reaches Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_lpa:,.0f}"` at a simulated mean
of `{python} f"{lpa_ds_mean:.3f}"` ppm, which is `{python} f"{lpa_ds_ratio:,.0f}"`-fold
below the criterion. An index of that size should be read as showing only that the attribute does not constrain the process, with @tbl-cap reporting it for completeness.

Two bounds apply to these figures. They describe operation within the normal operating range and say nothing about the excursion corners discussed in §6. They also rest on the scale-down model and on the process model behind the simulation, neither of which represents the resin life-cycle. The tightest capability anywhere in the drug substance is
`{python} f"{V['min_cpk']:.2f}"`, which belongs to a viral clearance attribute that this
step makes no claim on (PCMR-001).

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified under SOP-4001 from the demonstrated effects in §5 and from
the risk of leaving the design space in routine operation. The outcome is carried in @tbl-params, with the rationale for each parameter set out below.

- Protein load is classified as a well-controlled critical process parameter. Load carries
  the second largest coefficient on pool host cell protein and interacts with elution
  buffer pH (@tbl-coef-hcp). Because the NOR-propagated proven acceptable range for load,
  `{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','load','PAR (NOR)')` g/L resin, does not cover the
  upper part of the normal operating range, the parameter is linked to a critical quality
  attribute and bounds the operating region. Load is set by a mass calculation from a
  measured feed titre and is readily controlled, which keeps the risk of leaving the design
  space low and makes the class well-controlled critical instead of critical.

- Elution buffer pH is classified as a well-controlled critical process parameter. Elution
  pH carries the largest coefficient of any term on pool host cell protein and the only significant curvature. However, the NOR-propagated proven acceptable range for elution pH, `{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','elution_ph','PAR (NOR)')`, does not cover the low part of the normal operating range. Buffer pH is prepared and released against a
  specification before use. The deviation in §13.1 shows both that the control can fail and
  that release testing detects it, which is what a well-controlled parameter means here.

- Load flow rate is classified as a key process parameter, since flow affects step yield significantly and reduces it at high load through the load by flow interaction, while
  reaching no significant effect on pool host cell protein in either design. The NOR-propagated proven acceptable range for flow, `{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','flow','PAR (NOR)')` cm/hr, covers the whole of the normal operating range. The parameter therefore governs process performance without constraining
  a quality attribute, which is the key process parameter class.

- End of pool collect is classified as a key process parameter, since collect volume carries the dominant effect on step yield and also reaches significance on pool host cell protein in
  the response-surface model, at `{python} f"{rcoef('pool_hcp_ng_mg','D'):,.0f}"` ng/mg per
  coded unit, smaller than the elution pH coefficient by a factor of
  `{python} f"{d_vs_b_hcp:.0f}"`. Because the
  NOR-propagated proven acceptable range,
  `{python} par_cell('pool_hcp_ng_mg','end_collect','PAR (NOR)')` CV, covers the whole
  normal operating range, the effect is real without bounding the region. The parameter is
  classified as key on that basis and is monitored as a performance parameter.

- Operating temperature is classified as a general process parameter. It was assessed one
  parameter at a time over
  `{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('temperature').prange[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('temperature').prange[1]:g}"` °C
  and was not linked to any governed attribute. In operation it is held within a narrow band by the chromatography chamber EQ-CHR-118.

- Bed height is classified as a general process parameter. It was assessed one parameter at
  a time over
  `{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('bed_height').prange[0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('bed_height').prange[1]:g}"` cm,
  acts only through residence time at a fixed linear velocity, and is fixed in operation by
  the packing acceptance criteria in SOP-2008.

The classification returns `{python} n_cpp` critical process parameters at this step, against `{python} n_wccpp` well-controlled critical, `{python} n_kpp` key and `{python} n_gpp` general. The absence of a critical process parameter follows from
control capability and not from an absence of effect. Both well-controlled critical
parameters have a demonstrated effect on a critical quality attribute, while both are held by instrumentation and by released buffers that make an excursion outside the design space unlikely and detectable. In addition, the two key process parameters are held to the normal operating ranges for consistency of yield and pool volume, which is the reason a parameter with no demonstrated link to a quality attribute is nonetheless part of the control strategy [@amab2009].

# Contribution to the control strategy

Step `{python} step_no` contributes six elements to the control strategy for the drug
substance, stated here in the order a batch encounters them.

Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within the normal operating ranges and jointly within the design space of §6. The joint constraint is the operative one, which is
why the batch record carries it as a combined limit instead of as two independent ranges.
Load flow rate and end of pool collect are controlled within their normal operating ranges as key process parameters, which assures consistent yield and pool volume without being
linked to a quality attribute.

Pool host cell protein is monitored on every batch against the in-process limit of
`{python} f"{hcp_ipc:,.0f}"` ng/mg by AMV-3012. A result above that limit is an alert that
triggers assessment against the downstream clearance actually available, since the limit
sits `{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"`-fold below the concentration at which the train can no
longer bring a batch into specification.

Leached Protein A is measured on the capture pool of every batch by AMV-3016 and trended
against resin cycle number. This is the control that carries the attribute, because the
characterization studies found no operating parameter that governs it (§5.3). Resin
life-cycle limits, packing acceptance criteria and the sanitization sequence are held under SOP-2008. The batch trend is the evidence that leaching stays inside the criterion as the resin ages.

Elution buffer preparation is controlled by release testing against a pH specification before the buffer is used. The deviation in §13.1 arose in buffer preparation and was detected by that release test, which is the reason the control is named here as a contribution of the step. Finally, the four multivariate parameters are recorded on the batch record with the design-space constraint attached to the pair of quality-linked parameters, which allows a reviewer at disposition to see whether the batch was operated inside the region defined in §6.

The step does not control any of the three governed attributes alone: cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008) deliver the majority of the host cell protein clearance and both clear leached Protein A, while anion exchange delivers the majority of
the DNA clearance. No viral clearance is claimed here. The consolidated control strategy,
including the cumulative clearance and the parameter classes across the whole train, is
given in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is well understood over the ranges studied, although the understanding is distributed unevenly across the three responses. Pool host cell protein is described
by a predictive model with a clear mechanism, an interaction and a curvature, which makes
it the response that defines the operating region. Step yield is described adequately and matters for process consistency rather than for quality, whereas leached Protein A is described by no model at all. What is known about the attribute comes from the assayed pools and from the resin life-cycle programme.

The finding that deserves the most attention is the gap between the normal operating range
and the design space. `{python} pct(1 - nor_ok)` of the normal operating range exceeds the
in-process limit for pool host cell protein on the fitted model, at the corner where a
heavy load meets a low elution pH. Three things bound that finding, and none of them removes it: the in-process limit carries an assurance factor of
`{python} f"{hcp_margin:g}"`. The drug substance stays within specification even at that
corner, at `{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst_ds:.0f}"` ng/mg against
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_lim:.0f}"`. And the corner requires two parameters to sit at
unfavourable edges simultaneously, which routine operation at the set-point does not
approach. The response is to state the constraint jointly in §6 and §10, and to keep the
in-process monitor as the point of detection.

Confidence in the scale-down model rests on the qualification described in §3.1 and on the
agreement between the two independently executed designs. The screening and
response-surface models agree on the sign and approximate size of every large effect,
having been executed as separate campaigns on the same configuration. The one
disagreement, on end of pool collect against pool host cell protein, is between a
non-significant screening estimate and a significant response-surface estimate. The disagreement is resolved in favour of the design that can resolve it.

Both deviations recorded in §13 were analytical or preparative in origin and neither
altered a dataset. The elution buffer prepared below target delivered a pH of
`{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:g}"`, which sits inside the characterization range at a coded position of `{python} f"{dev_ph_coded:.2f}"`. The leached Protein A result that was initially out of trend was assayed again at
`{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:g}"` ppm. Both runs were retained, with the impact
assessments given in §13.

Four limitations apply to the conclusions of this report. The response-surface models
predict mean levels and carry no interval of their own, which is why the assurance form of
the range claim is the NOR-propagated analysis in §7 and why the design-space boundary
should not be treated as a point of high reliability. A single feed state drawn from material characterized in PCR-004 was used in both designs, which leaves the effect of feed variability on this step bounded by that document instead of by this one. Both designs were run at a single resin lot and cycle count, which leaves leaching over the resin lifetime to SOP-2008 and to the
batch trend described in §10. And the design space was verified at scale-down and not at commercial scale at the edges of the region, which is a general limitation of the approach [@amab2009].

No parameter at this step required the most stringent control class. Both quality-linked
parameters are held by instrumentation and by released buffers with a low risk of leaving
the design space, which is what distinguishes a well-controlled critical process parameter from a critical one under SOP-4001. Overall, the picture is of a step whose quality-relevant behaviour is concentrated in two parameters and whose remaining variation is either analytical or attributable to the resin, which is a simpler control problem than the parameter count of @tbl-params suggests.

# Conclusions

Protein A chromatography has been characterized at commercial-equivalent scale-down over
`{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_multi` of them in a screening design of
`{python} n_scr` runs followed by a response-surface design of `{python} n_rsm` runs. The
step is well understood and robust within the ranges studied.

A multivariate design space has been defined in protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow
rate and end of pool collect, covering `{python} pct(ds_frac)` of the characterized region
and bounded by pool host cell protein at high load and low elution pH. Protein load and
elution buffer pH must be held jointly inside that region, since neither NOR-propagated
proven acceptable range covers the whole of the corresponding routine range.

All `{python} n_pools` capture pools met the leached Protein A criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm, at a maximum of `{python} f"{lpa_max:.2f}"` ppm, with no
operating parameter identified as governing the attribute. At commercial scale the three governed attributes meet the drug-substance criteria, and the tightest of them is `{python} cpk_tight_name` at Cpk `{python} f"{cpk_tight:.1f}"`.

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_wccpp` were classified as well-controlled critical,
`{python} n_kpp` as key and `{python} n_gpp` as general, with `{python} n_cpp` classified as
critical. Two deviations were investigated and resolved without effect on the models,
the region or the classifications.

The step does not deliver the drug-substance host cell protein specification on its own, nor does it carry a viral clearance claim. These conclusions are rolled up into PCMR-001, which consolidates the design spaces, capabilities and classifications of the whole train.

# Deviations from the plan

Two deviations were recorded during execution of PCP-005, each of them investigated to root cause, impact-assessed against the affected datasets and dispositioned as retained, and @tbl-dev summarizes the two.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print("\n: Deviations recorded during execution of PCP-005. {#tbl-dev}\n")
```

## Elution buffer prepared below target (DEV-005-01)

An elution buffer lot, LOT-BUF-5290, was prepared below the target pH and was used on one run of the response-surface design. A pH of `{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:g}"` was measured at release testing, against a target of `{python} f"{SP['elution_ph']:g}"` for the centre-point condition. Because elution buffer
pH carries the largest coefficient of any term on pool host cell protein (§5.3), a
departure in this parameter is the most consequential preparation error the step can make.

The root cause was identified during the investigation as a titration endpoint error in preparation.
The pH meter was within calibration, the buffer components were within specification and the endpoint was called early by the operator. Retraining and a second-person verification at the endpoint were implemented for all subsequent buffer preparations.

The impact assessment turned on where the delivered pH falls. A pH of
`{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:g}"` sits inside the characterization range of
`{python} f"{PR['elution_ph'][0]:g}"`–`{python} f"{PR['elution_ph'][1]:g}"` at a coded position of `{python} f"{dev_ph_coded:.2f}"`. Consequently, the run remained inside the region the response-surface model covers, with no extrapolation introduced. The affected run was analysed at the delivered setting and the deviation was dispositioned as retained. Lack of
fit for pool host cell protein remains non-significant (@tbl-lof-hcp), which is the
statistical evidence that the affected run is consistent with the fitted surface.

## Leached Protein A result initially out of trend (DEV-005-02)

A leached Protein A result was reported out of trend against the other pools of the
campaign and was raised at analytical review. The value fell outside the range the
remaining pools occupied, which for this response is a wide range: the campaign spans
`{python} f"{lpa_min:.2f}"` to `{python} f"{lpa_max:.2f}"` ppm with a centre-point
coefficient of variation of `{python} f"{cvr('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.1f}"` %.

The probable cause was identified in the assay sequence as suspected carry-over between adjacent wells. The sample was assayed again under AMV-3016 and returned `{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:g}"` ppm, which meets the acceptance criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm by a wide margin. The validated intermediate precision of the method is
`{python} f"{lpa_prec:g}"` %RSD with a limit of quantitation of
`{python} f"{lpa_loq:g}"` ppm, and `{python} f"{100*lpa_varfrac:.0f}"` % of the total observed variance in this response is attributable to the assay itself (Appendix D, @tbl-appd). Sequence
controls and a bracketing blank were added to the routine sequence of the method.

The run was retained, and the impact on this report is limited by the treatment of the attribute in §5.3, since no predictive model is fitted to leached Protein A and the
operative claim is that all `{python} n_pools` assayed pools met the criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_lim:.0f}"` ppm. A re-assayed result of `{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:g}"` ppm does not approach that criterion and does not change the conclusion. Neither of the two deviations altered a classification, a proven acceptable range or the design space.

## Appendix C — Full effect and coefficient tables

@tbl-appc1 to @tbl-appc3 give every screening effect estimate for the three responses.
@tbl-appc4 and @tbl-appc5 give the full quadratic coefficients for the two responses not
tabulated in §5.3, and @tbl-appc6 and @tbl-appc7 give the corresponding analysis of
variance.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"))
print("\n: All screening effect estimates for pool host cell protein. {#tbl-appc1}\n")

print("\n: All screening effect estimates for step yield. {#tbl-appc2}\n")
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"))
print("\n: All screening effect estimates for leached Protein A. {#tbl-appc3}\n")
show(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "step_yield"))
print("\n: Full quadratic coefficients for step yield. {#tbl-appc4}\n")
show(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"))
print("\n: Full quadratic coefficients for leached Protein A. {#tbl-appc5}\n")
show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "step_yield"))

show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"))
print("\n: Analysis of variance for leached Protein A. {#tbl-appc7}\n")
```
